project.name: dynamic-sdui-app
project.description: An experimental Angular 21 + Genkit framework for AI-powered Server-Driven UI (SDUI). Two-AI architecture: a Generator AI (Python MCP CLI) scaffolds app assets at dev time, and an Executor AI (Genkit generateUIFlow behind POST /generateUI) streams component schemas that MagicAiRenderer instantiates imperatively at runtime from user chat intent. Ships three demo apps (vacation-rentals, magic-bookstore, adev-docs).

nodes.name: MagicAiComponent

nodes.name: magic-ai-renderer.component.ts
nodes.summary: The core SDUI rendering engine: recursively traverses a DynamicSchema tree and imperatively instantiates Angular components, HTML elements, or text nodes — creating components with input bindings via createComponent and attaching them to Angular's change detection.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Angular's imperative createComponent API with inputBinding, ApplicationRef.attachView, and a reactive effect to tear down and re-render the entire subtree whenever the schema signal changes — a rare low-level pattern that bypasses the template compiler.

nodes.name: MagicAiRenderer
nodes.summary: Accepts a DynamicSchema input signal and imperatively renders a tree of Angular components ('componentSchema'), HTML elements ('elementSchema'), or text nodes ('textSchema'), cleaning up destroyed views on schema change.

nodes.name: magic-ai.service.ts
nodes.summary: Root-level Angular service that drives the SDUI AI loop: streams component schemas from the Genkit 'generateUI' flow using Angular's resource API, maintains a paginated componentSchemaList via linkedSignal, and rotates loading placeholder text during generation.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Angular 21's experimental resource() with streaming and linkedSignal() — advanced reactive primitives that keep the schema list incrementally updated as the Genkit stream emits partial responses.

nodes.name: MagicAiService
nodes.summary: Injectable service providing the SDUI prompt signal, the streaming componentResource backed by Genkit, and derived signals (componentSchemaList, isStreamComplete, loadingText) consumed by the container and chat components.

nodes.name: flows.ts

nodes.languageNotes: Uses Genkit's `ai.defineFlow` and `ai.generateStream` with Zod schemas for structured output, enabling streaming JSON conforming to the SDUI component schema.

nodes.name: generateUIFlow

nodes.languageNotes: The prompt is a 164-line template literal covering a 6-section instruction set: role, inputs, generation process, layout primitives, styling guidelines, and output schema.

nodes.name: server.ts

nodes.languageNotes: Combines Genkit's `expressHandler` adapter with Angular's `AngularNodeAppEngine` for SSR in a single Express process, enabling both AI API calls and SSR from one server.

nodes.name: POST /generateUI
nodes.summary: HTTP endpoint that accepts POST requests and delegates to the `generateUIFlow` Genkit flow, streaming AI-generated SDUI component schemas back to the client.

nodes.name: server.py
nodes.summary: The Generator-AI half of the two-AI architecture: a FastMCP server that exposes two interactive scaffolding prompts to a Gemini CLI user, guiding them step-by-step through either generating a complete new SDUI application (app-context, Angular components, showcase, and global registry updates) or adding a single new component to an existing SDUI app, including design guidelines, code-generation rules, and an automated build-verify-fix loop.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses FastMCP's @mcp.prompt decorator pattern — each decorated function returns a large multi-step instruction string rather than executing logic directly; the LLM (Gemini CLI) interprets and executes those instructions against the project files.

nodes.summary: Global stylesheet that imports Tailwind CSS and a syntax-highlighting theme, then defines per-app CSS custom property namespaces (haven, adev-docs, magic-bookstore, vacation-rentals) with full design token sets, plus corresponding theme classes that map the namespaced tokens to generic CSS variables consumed by all dynamic components.
nodes.languageNotes: The per-app theme variables (e.g., --haven-primary) are namespaced to avoid collisions, then remapped to generic --primary, --background, etc. inside scoped theme classes; this is the CSS-variable theming contract that all generated components depend on.

layers.name: SDUI Runtime Core
layers.description: The Angular 21 client-side engine that streams AI-generated component schemas, imperatively instantiates registered components via createComponent, and manages the persistent AI chat sidebar — the heart of the server-driven UI loop.

layers.name: Executor AI Backend (Genkit)
layers.description: The Node.js/Express server and Genkit utilities that run the Executor AI: defines the generateUIFlow Genkit flow streaming Gemini-generated SDUI schemas over HTTP, manages session history, aggregates per-app data for AI context, and exposes the POST /generateUI endpoint consumed by the Angular client.

layers.name: Generator AI (MCP Server)
layers.description: The Python FastMCP server that acts as the dev-time Generator AI, exposing scaffolding prompts to a Gemini CLI user for interactively creating new SDUI demo apps or adding individual components, including automated build-verify-fix loops.

layers.name: Demo App: Vacation Rentals
layers.description: Self-contained SDUI demo application simulating a vacation rental marketplace with 19 standalone Angular components (property cards, booking widget, listing headers, gallery, reviews, etc.), a signal-based favorites service, and typed fixture data — all registered in the app-context so the AI can instantiate them dynamically.

layers.name: Demo App: Magic Bookstore
layers.description: Self-contained SDUI demo application for an AI-powered bookstore with 14 standalone Angular components (book covers, author bios, reviews, carousels, genre tags, stock availability, etc.), a comprehensive catalog data-store, and a showcase component — all registered in the app-context for dynamic AI rendering.

layers.name: Demo App: Angular Dev Docs
layers.description: Self-contained SDUI demo application that renders AI-generated Angular documentation pages using 10 standalone Angular components (API reference, callouts, code snippets, concept explanations, topic cards, etc.), a markdown knowledge-base data-store, and a showcase — illustrating how SDUI can drive interactive documentation experiences.

layers.name: App Bootstrap & Configuration
layers.description: Angular application entry points, SSR configuration, route declarations, global styles, build tooling configs, and project documentation that wire together the full application — including browser and server bootstrap files, Angular workspace config, TypeScript project references, and the Tailwind PostCSS pipeline.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README introduces this experimental framework for AI-powered Server-Driven UI. It describes the two-AI architecture: a Python-based Generator AI (MCP CLI) that scaffolds app assets at dev time, and a Genkit Executor AI that renders UIs dynamically at runtime from user chat intent. Reading this first gives you the mental model for everything that follows.

tour.title: App Bootstrap & Shell
tour.description: Bootstrap begins in `main.ts`, which calls `bootstrapApplication` with `AppComponent` and the provider config from `app.config.ts`. `AppComponent` is a thin shell with a `<router-outlet>`, and `app.routes.ts` maps URL paths to lazy-loaded components — including the critical `/magic-ai` route that hosts the SDUI engine. These three files together define the application's outer frame.
tour.languageLesson: Angular 21 uses standalone components throughout — there are no NgModules. `bootstrapApplication` wires providers directly, and routes lazy-load standalone components with `loadComponent`, keeping bundles small.

tour.title: Layout & Persistent Chat Sidebar
tour.description: `base.component.ts` is the layout wrapper that wraps every demo app route. It renders the main content area alongside a persistent AI chat sidebar, ensuring the chat UI is always visible regardless of which demo app is active. This is the structural container that makes the 'ambient AI' experience possible.

tour.title: Chat UI & Chat Service
tour.description: `chat.component.ts` renders the conversation panel — displaying message history and the user's text input. `chat.service.ts` is the hub that bridges component-level user interactions to the AI layer: it calls `MagicAiService.setPrompt()`, appends to the conversation history, and navigates the router to the chat view. Any component anywhere in the app can call `ChatService.addUserPrompt()` to kick off an AI interaction.
tour.languageLesson: With fan-in of 12, `chat.service.ts` is the most-imported file in the codebase. Demo app components (PropertyCard, DestinationCard, ViewDetailsButton) all call `addUserPrompt()` to inject AI prompts from user clicks — a clean inversion of control.

tour.title: MagicAiService: Streaming Schemas from the Backend
tour.description: `magic-ai.service.ts` is the Angular client that communicates with the Executor AI backend. It uses Angular's reactive `resource()` API to stream the AI-generated component schema from `POST /generateUI` as the user's prompt changes. The streamed response is a structured JSON array describing which SDUI components to render and with what inputs — the core runtime contract of the entire framework.
tour.languageLesson: Angular 21's `resource()` function is a signals-native async primitive that handles loading, error, and data states automatically. Unlike RxJS `HttpClient`, it re-fetches reactively when its request signal changes — perfect for streaming AI responses tied to a chat prompt signal.

tour.title: MagicAiRenderer: Imperative Component Instantiation
tour.description: `magic-ai-renderer.component.ts` takes the schema array emitted by `MagicAiService` and imperatively instantiates real Angular components using `createComponent`. It looks up each schema entry's `componentType` in the app context registry, creates the component in a `ViewContainerRef`, and sets its `@Input()` properties from the schema's `inputs` object. This is where the AI's abstract specification becomes live Angular UI.
tour.languageLesson: Angular's `createComponent()` API allows fully imperative, dynamic component creation at runtime without a template. Combined with `setInput()`, it enables a generic renderer that can instantiate any registered component the AI specifies — the key capability making SDUI possible.

tour.title: MagicAiContainer: Routing & Pagination
tour.description: `magic-ai-container.component.ts` is the routed view that hosts `MagicAiRenderer`. It manages pagination across multi-page AI responses and coordinates the top-level layout of the AI-rendered content area. It imports both `MagicAiRenderer` and `MagicAiService`, acting as the orchestration layer between the router, the renderer, and the streaming service.

tour.title: Executor AI Entry Point: server.ts & POST /generateUI
tour.description: `server.ts` is the Node.js/Express server that runs alongside the Angular SSR app. It exposes the `POST /generateUI` endpoint that Angular's `MagicAiService` calls. When a request arrives, this endpoint delegates to the `generateUIFlow` Genkit flow — the actual AI logic — and streams the response back to the client.
tour.languageLesson: Angular's `angular.json` configures `server.ts` as the SSR server entry. This means the same process that serves Angular SSR pages also runs the Express AI endpoint, eliminating the need for a separate backend deployment.

tour.title: Executor AI Logic: generateUIFlow & Prompts
tour.description: `flows.ts` defines `generateUIFlow`, the Genkit flow that calls Gemini to produce the SDUI schema. It receives the user's intent and the app's component registry, constructs the context using `prompts.ts`, calls Gemini, and streams back a structured JSON array of `{componentType, inputs}` objects. `prompts.ts` contains the system prompt templates that instruct Gemini on the output format and available component types.
tour.languageLesson: Genkit flows are typed, observable AI pipelines. `defineFlow` wraps the Gemini call with input/output schema validation (Zod), streaming support, and built-in tracing — making the AI call debuggable and type-safe end to end.

tour.title: Executor AI Data Store: Aggregating Context
tour.description: `src/genkit-utils/data-store.ts` aggregates the fixture data from all three demo apps and the component registry from `app-context.ts`. This aggregated context is injected into the Gemini prompt so the AI knows what real data exists and what components are available to render it. It is the bridge between the frontend component catalog and the backend AI prompt.

tour.title: App Context: The Component Registry Contract
tour.description: `src/app/magic-ai/app-context.ts` is the central runtime registry that aggregates all three demo apps' component catalogs into a single lookup map. Each entry maps a string component type name to the actual Angular component class and its JSON schema. `MagicAiRenderer` reads this registry at render time; `genkit-utils/data-store.ts` reads it at prompt-construction time — it is the shared contract between the AI and the renderer.

tour.title: Demo App: Vacation Rentals
tour.description: The vacation-rentals demo illustrates the complete SDUI pattern end to end. `vacation-rentals/app-context.ts` registers 19 standalone components with their JSON schemas, making them available to the AI. `data-store.ts` provides typed fixture listings, hosts, and reviews that the Executor AI uses as grounded context. Representative components like `property-card.component.ts` and `booking-widget.component.ts` show how components call `ChatService.addUserPrompt()` to trigger further AI navigation — creating an AI-native interactive loop.

tour.title: Generator AI: MCP Scaffolding Server
tour.description: `mcp-server/server.py` is the Python FastMCP server that acts as the dev-time Generator AI. It exposes scaffolding prompts (`generate_dynamic_sdui_app`, `create_dynamic_component`) to a Gemini CLI user, automating the creation of new SDUI demo apps with build-verify-fix loops. This is how the vacation-rentals and bookstore demo apps were themselves generated — completing the two-AI story.
tour.languageLesson: FastMCP exposes Python functions as MCP tools consumable by any MCP-compatible AI client (e.g., Gemini CLI). The `@mcp.tool()` decorator registers a function with its docstring as the tool description, making the Generator AI a purely declarative scaffolding interface.

tour.title: Build Config & Global Theming
tour.description: `angular.json` and `package.json` define the build pipeline: the Angular CLI compiles the browser bundle and the SSR server bundle together, with `server.ts` as the custom server entry. `styles.css` establishes the Tailwind CSS baseline and any global CSS custom properties that define the visual theming contract shared across all demo apps — the styling foundation the AI-rendered components inherit.
tour.languageLesson: Tailwind with PostCSS (`.postcssrc.json`) processes `styles.css` at build time, purging unused utility classes from the final bundle. Since SDUI components are instantiated dynamically, component template strings must reference complete Tailwind class names (not dynamically constructed strings) to survive the purge step.
